I wrote the 30-minute lesson on O3, `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`, plus a short quiz and its key. I haven't opened the lesson in a browser. I also couldn't run a word count, so I'm estimating it at about 3,500 words, inside the 2,700–6,750 range that fits 30 minutes.

**The win:** you can decide what the makerspace assistant keeps in its context, what it saves between visits, and how it finds the right page in a long manual.

**What the lesson covers:**
- **The context window:** what goes into it and what counts toward it, and tokens, defined for the first time. It also covers why a bigger window isn't a reason to stuff it.
- **Between steps:** the model is blank on every call, so the program resends the whole history. This is why cost grows with each step.
- **When the context fills up:** clearing old tool results, compaction and sub-agents.
- **Between sessions:** saving notes or records outside the context and loading them back. It covers when to use a database and when to use model-written notes.
- **Retrieval:** chunking, searching and handing over a few passages, with `search_manuals` as the just-in-time example.
- **Practice:** a worked example following Sam's booking request, and a faded exercise on Priya's warping print. It also has three figures and five checks with instant feedback.

**Sources:** the primary one is Anthropic's [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents). It also draws on the Claude docs pages on context windows and the memory tool, and Anthropic's contextual retrieval post. I added all four to `RESOURCES.md`.

**Quiz 0002** (five items on O3) is ready whenever you are; ask me for it. I also updated `NOTES.md`. Quiz 0001 still hasn't been graded, so I haven't written any learning record from this lesson yet.

One question for you: do you want me to build a one-page cheat sheet of the "load, retrieve, save" decisions for your design review?
